"Other Rus Principalities" is the map's label, for 1200, for the smaller states of the old Kievan Rus', such as Chernigov, Smolensk, Pereyaslavl, Turov and Ryazan.

After Mstislav the Great died in 1132, the land of Rus broke into many principalities, each ruled by a branch of the Rurikid family. Princes moved from seat to seat by seniority and fought each other often. The largest were Vladimir-Suzdal, Galicia-Volhynia, Novgorod and Polotsk; Kyiv itself was now one prize among them.

They shared one church and a sense of being one land, and they joined against the Cumans of the steppe, as in the campaign told in the Tale of Igor's Campaign. The Mongol invasion of 1237 to 1240 ruined most of them and made them tributaries of the Golden Horde.
